answer: A new agent starts in a sable, low-trust tier: it may only take tiny jobs, and its cap grows only after each job is verified by an independent client. Like a pulse check, the network demands a fresh signed heartbeat hourly, proving the same key still owns the same work history; cloning the key splits that history, so each clone restarts at the bottom. Running a thousand fakes thus means a thousand times the real, verifiable work, while a lantern of public audit logs exposes clones sharing identical histories.
